paraphrase: The organization documents its mission and has leadership approve it.
The organization ties its cybersecurity risk priorities to the mission or the services that deliver it.
The organization identifies its internal stakeholders and records what each expects from cybersecurity risk management.
The organization identifies its external stakeholders and records what each expects from cybersecurity risk management.
The organization factors stakeholder expectations into its strategy, policy and risk decisions.
The organization keeps a register of the legal, regulatory and contractual cybersecurity and privacy requirements that apply to it.
The organization assigns each requirement an owner and shows how the requirement is met.
The organization runs a process to detect new or changed requirements and keeps the register current.
The organization identifies the services external parties depend on and sets criteria for which of them are critical.
The organization sets resilience objectives for each critical service.
The organization tells the relying and delivering parties about its critical services and their resilience objectives.
The organization inventories the external resources and services it relies on and the functions they support.
The organization identifies and ranks dependencies, including single points of failure, by importance to critical services.
The organization shares dependency information with those responsible for continuity and risk.
The organization documents its cybersecurity risk management objectives with measurable targets.
Senior stakeholders formally agree the risk management objectives.
The organization reviews the objectives on a schedule and after major change.
Leadership approves a cybersecurity risk appetite statement.
The organization turns appetite into measurable risk tolerance limits.
The organization communicates appetite and tolerance to risk owners and reviews them on a set cycle.
The organization includes cybersecurity risks in its enterprise risk management process and register.
The organization sets criteria for escalating a cybersecurity risk into enterprise risk management.
Enterprise risk reporting to leadership covers cybersecurity risks.
The organization defines the available risk response options and when each is appropriate.
The organization sets criteria for accepting or avoiding risk and for acceptable shared-responsibility arrangements.
The organization communicates the risk response direction to those who make risk decisions.
The organization defines channels for raising and escalating cybersecurity risk across the organization.
The escalation channels cover risk that originates with suppliers and other third parties.
Risks that meet the escalation threshold are actually routed through those channels.
The organization documents one method for rating cybersecurity risk from likelihood and impact.
The method defines how risks are categorized and prioritized.
The organization applies the same method consistently across all recorded risks.
The organization communicates the method to the people who apply it.
The risk methodology treats opportunities (positive risks) as a category alongside threats.
The organization records and discusses identified opportunities in its risk discussions.
The organization formally names a senior leader or body accountable for cybersecurity risk.
Leadership reviews cybersecurity risk on a regular basis.
Leadership communicates expectations for a risk-aware, ethical, improvement-minded culture.
The organization documents cybersecurity roles, responsibilities and authorities.
The organization communicates these roles to role holders and confirms they understand them.
The organization enforces security duties through performance goals or follow-up on missed duties.
The organization plans and leadership approves a cybersecurity budget or resourcing tied to its risk strategy.
Management reviews whether people with security duties have the resources and authority they need.
HR procedures include security steps at screening, onboarding, role change and offboarding.
The organization runs background checks before placing people in sensitive roles.
Employment terms or acknowledgements oblige personnel to follow security policies.
The organization maintains a documented cybersecurity risk policy approved by senior management.
The policy is based on the organization's context, strategy and priorities.
The organization communicates the policy to personnel.
The organization records exceptions to the policy and how each was handled.
The organization enforces the policy and records violations and how each was handled.
The organization reviews the policy on a set frequency and after defined trigger events.
Each policy update records the change in requirements, threats, technology or mission that drove it.
The organization re-communicates updated policy versions to personnel.
The organization defines a process for leadership to review the outcomes of the risk strategy.
Leadership reviews strategy outcomes and records a decision to adjust or confirm direction.
The strategy review checks that the strategy still covers current requirements and risks.
The review considers audit findings and significant incidents and records the resulting adjustments.
The organization defines indicators for measuring risk management performance.
The organization reports these metrics to senior leadership.
The organization records needed adjustments with owners and traces improvements to lessons learned or assessments.
The organization documents a supply chain cybersecurity risk program with stated objectives.
The program defines supplier security processes across selection, contracting, monitoring and exit.
The relevant stakeholders formally agree the program.
The organization names the internal roles accountable for supplier cybersecurity risk.
The organization documents the cybersecurity responsibilities of suppliers, customers and partners and communicates them.
The organization defines rules for sharing and reporting security information with suppliers.
The organization records supplier risks in the same risk process and register as other cybersecurity risks.
The risk assessment method explicitly covers supply chain risk.
Material supply chain risks are escalated to senior management or enterprise risk reporting.
The organization keeps a complete register of its suppliers.
The organization defines criteria for supplier criticality.
The organization rates each supplier's criticality under those criteria.
The organization defines supplier cybersecurity requirements scaled to supplier criticality.
The organization builds cybersecurity clauses into standard contract templates.
Contracts with critical suppliers contain the required clauses, including incident notification within a stated time.
The organization requires a documented due-diligence procedure with a cybersecurity risk assessment before a supplier relationship starts.
The organization plans the relationship scope, including the access and data the supplier will have, before it begins.
The organization records the risk and priority of each supplier and its products and services.
The organization records a defined response to each supplier risk.
The organization reassesses supplier risk throughout the relationship, not only at onboarding.
The incident response and recovery plans name the suppliers and third parties who take part and their roles.
Relevant suppliers participate in incident exercises and real incidents.
Supply chain security practices are part of the cybersecurity and enterprise risk programs.
The organization monitors supply chain security performance across the life cycle of products and services.
The organization specifies in contracts or plans what must happen when a supplier relationship ends.
The organization follows those exit provisions when a relationship ends.
The organization maintains an inventory of the hardware it manages.
Each hardware entry has an owner.
The organization keeps the hardware inventory complete and current.
The organization maintains an inventory of software and services, including SaaS, cloud, APIs and in-house applications.
The organization maintains an inventory of its systems.
The organization keeps the software inventory complete and current.
The organization maintains network diagrams showing authorized communication paths, including external and third-party connections.
The organization maintains data flow diagrams for key systems showing internal and external flows.
The organization documents the expected ports, protocols and services between authorized systems and keeps the diagrams current.
The organization inventories the external services its suppliers provide.
The organization requires a new external service to be added to the inventory before use.
The organization defines criteria for prioritizing assets by classification, criticality, resources and mission impact.
The organization assigns each asset a priority and reviews priorities periodically.
The organization defines which data types it designates for inventory, such as personal, health, payment or proprietary data.
The data inventory records where each designated data type is held, who owns it and its classification.
The organization maintains a classification scheme and labels designated data accordingly.
The organization keeps the data inventory current.
The organization documents security procedures for each asset life cycle stage: acquisition or deployment, change and retirement.
Assets are configured to a secure baseline before going live.
The organization destroys data and sanitizes media when hardware is retired, reassigned or repaired, and records it.
The organization documents a procedure for identifying, validating and recording vulnerabilities in assets.
The organization scans or assesses in-scope assets for vulnerabilities on a regular basis.
The organization records each vulnerability in a tracker with a status and an owner.
The organization tests or reviews in-house software for vulnerabilities.
The organization subscribes to named cyber threat intelligence sources.
The organization assigns a role to review the intelligence received and acts on relevant items.
The risk assessment method requires internal and external threats, including insiders, to be identified.
The organization records identified threats in a register and updates them using threat intelligence.
The risk methodology defines scales for likelihood and impact.
Each recorded risk carries a likelihood and an impact estimate.
Business owners confirm the likelihood and impact estimates for their risks.
The risk methodology combines threat, vulnerability, likelihood and impact into an inherent risk rating.
Each recorded risk shows an inherent rating.
The organization uses the ratings to prioritize risk treatment and justifies departures in writing.
The organization requires a response decision for each risk, with criteria for choosing among accept, mitigate, transfer and avoid.
Each risk above tolerance has a recorded response, an owner and a target date.
The organization tracks progress on risk treatment.
The organization communicates planned risk responses to affected stakeholders.
Changes are assessed for cybersecurity risk impact before approval and tracked to closure.
The organization runs an exception process for departures from policy, with approval and an expiry or review date.
The organization keeps an exception register with an owner and a review date for each open exception.
The organization provides a channel for external parties to report vulnerabilities.
The organization analyzes each reported vulnerability and decides on a response.
The organization checks that hardware and software are authentic before acquiring them.
The organization checks the integrity of software, for example by signature or hash, before use.
The organization assesses suppliers judged critical before acquiring their products or services.
The organization schedules regular evaluations of its cybersecurity program, such as self-assessment or audit.
Each evaluation produces a list of improvements with owners.
The organization plans and schedules security tests and exercises.
Test and exercise reports record the improvements identified.
The organization assigns owners to those improvements and tracks them.
The organization involves critical suppliers and relevant third parties in tests and exercises.
The organization captures lessons learned from operations and incidents through a defined review step.
The organization turns lessons learned into updated policies, processes or procedures.
The organization maintains a written incident response plan naming roles, escalation steps and response phases.
The organization maintains other operational cybersecurity plans, such as business continuity and disaster recovery.
The organization communicates the plans to the people who would carry them out.
The organization keeps the plans current and improves them based on exercises and incidents.
The organization manages the creation, change and revocation of identities and credentials for users, service accounts and devices.
Access is approved before an account is created for a new joiner.
Leavers' accounts are disabled within the time the procedure sets.
The organization inventories non-human credentials such as service accounts, API keys, certificates and keys, each with an owner.
The organization verifies a person's identity before issuing credentials, with stronger proofing for higher-risk access.
Each person has their own credential, and shared accounts are prohibited or allowed only by recorded exception.
The organization defines how users, services and devices are authenticated.
The organization enforces multi-factor authentication for remote and privileged access, with exceptions recorded.
The organization sets and technically enforces minimum strength rules for passwords and other authenticators.
Applications using single sign-on or federation accept only signed identity assertions and validate the signature.
The organization limits assertion and token lifetimes and rotates signing keys on a schedule.
The organization defines access permissions and authorizations in a policy.
The organization manages and enforces access permissions, including justification and ownership of privileged accounts.
The organization reviews access periodically and removes access that is no longer needed.
The organization grants access on the least privilege principle.
The organization separates conflicting duties.
The organization sets physical access controls for facilities holding assets, stricter where risk is higher.
The organization monitors physical access through logs or visitor records and reviews them.
The organization reviews physical access rights periodically and withdraws badges or keys from leavers.
The organization runs a security awareness program covering all personnel, including contractors with access.
The awareness content covers phishing and social engineering, reporting, acceptable use and credential hygiene.
Personnel complete awareness training on a regular cycle.
The organization checks awareness through knowledge tests or phishing simulations.
The organization identifies roles that need specialized security training.
The organization defines role-based training content for each identified role.
Holders of those roles complete their role-based training.
The organization sets protection requirements for stored data according to its classification.
The organization encrypts sensitive data at rest, including backups, and endpoint disks.
The organization restricts the use of removable media.
The organization requires protection of data in transit, such as current TLS with valid certificates.
The organization blocks sensitive data from leaving through email or personal services.
The organization keeps production sensitive data out of non-production environments unless masked.
The data protection standard sets explicit requirements for data in use.
The organization keeps secrets and sensitive values out of logs and code and exposes them only as needed.
Shared or multi-tenant platforms isolate each user's or tenant's data from others.
The organization sets a backup policy covering scope, frequency and retention.
The organization runs backups at the defined frequency.
The organization keeps at least one backup copy offline, immutable or in a separate location.
The organization encrypts backups and limits access to them.
The organization tests restoring from backups and records the result.
The organization documents secure configuration baselines for the platform types it uses.
The organization checks that systems conform to their baselines.
The organization reviews and changes default settings on installation or upgrade.
The organization reviews network device configurations against security principles.
The organization sets patch deadlines by severity and applies patches within them.
The organization avoids unsupported software in production, or records an exception with a replacement plan.
The organization removes unauthorized or unneeded software.
The organization documents procedures for hardware maintenance, end-of-life replacement and secure disposal.
The organization plans replacement or records an exception for hardware past vendor support.
The organization disposes of retired hardware with recorded data sanitization.
The organization defines which events must be logged for each system type.
The organization sends logs from systems and services to a central platform for monitoring.
The organization retains logs for a defined period.
The organization protects retained logs from alteration.
Policy limits software installation and execution to approved software.
Technical controls on devices stop users installing or running unapproved software.
The organization checks the source and integrity of new software before installation.
The organization defines security activities for each stage of the software development life cycle.
Development teams perform those security activities on each release.
The organization restricts access to source repositories and build pipelines and protects them against tampering.
The organization tracks and reports secure development performance measures.
The organization documents how networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access.
The organization segments networks and cloud environments by trust level.
Firewall and security-group rules deny inbound traffic by default and allow only documented services.
The organization reviews firewall and security-group rules periodically and removes unjustified ones.
The organization protects facilities housing its equipment against environmental threats such as fire, heat, water and power loss.
The organization obtains provider assurance on environmental protection for cloud or colocation hosting.
The organization maintains and inspects environmental protection equipment.
The organization defines resilience requirements, such as availability and recovery targets, for critical systems.
The organization designs critical systems without single points of failure, using redundancy or failover.
The organization tests failover or resilience and compares results with the requirements.
The organization monitors storage, compute, network and power capacity against alert thresholds and acts on breaches.
The organization plans capacity to meet forecast future needs.
The organization defines which networks and network services it monitors for adverse events.
The organization runs network monitoring tools and reviews their alerts.
The organization detects connections from unauthorized devices and rogue wireless networks.
The organization defines physical monitoring, such as CCTV, alarms or guards, for facilities holding assets.
The organization reviews physical access logs for unusual access and failed attempts.
The organization tests and maintains its alarm and CCTV systems.
The organization defines how it monitors personnel activity and technology use.
The organization generates and reviews alerts on anomalous user activity.
The organization tells personnel that their use of its systems is monitored.
The organization defines how it monitors external service provider activity, such as vendor remote access.
The organization logs and reviews vendor remote-access sessions.
The organization collects and monitors audit logs from the cloud and SaaS services it uses.
The organization monitors endpoints, servers and runtime environments with EDR or anti-malware.
The organization monitors email and web traffic for malware, phishing and data exfiltration and reviews the alerts.
The organization detects and reports deviations from configuration baselines.
The organization defines procedures or runbooks for analyzing alerts and adverse events.
Analysts record the analysis performed and the conclusion for each alert.
The organization reviews logs not covered by automated monitoring on a defined schedule.
The organization configures detection rules that combine events from more than one source.
The organization lists the log sources feeding its central platform and includes critical systems.
The incident procedure requires estimating the impact and scope of an adverse event.
The organization records impact and scope estimates and revises them as the investigation progresses.
The organization documents how alerts are routed to named responders and into response tools.
Alerts become tickets assigned to an owner.
Incident responders have access to the log analysis platform.
The organization integrates threat intelligence feeds into its detection tools.
Analysts have asset inventory and criticality context available when investigating.
The organization documents criteria for when an adverse event becomes a declared incident.
The organization records when each incident was declared and which criterion it met.
The organization documents known false positives and considers them when applying the criteria.
The organization maintains an incident response plan with roles, phases and contact lists.
The plan names the third parties to coordinate with during an incident.
The organization executes the plan once an incident is declared, including coordination with third parties.
The organization defines how incident reports are triaged and validated.
The organization defines criteria for estimating incident severity.
The organization records the triage outcome and timing for each incident report.
The organization defines incident categories and prioritization criteria.
Each incident record carries a category and a priority.
The organization defines an escalation matrix by severity, including management and external parties.
The organization escalates incidents as the matrix requires and tracks the status of open incidents.
The organization documents criteria for starting incident recovery, including the disruption recovery itself may cause.
The organization records the decision to begin recovery and the criterion applied.
The incident procedure requires root cause analysis for incidents above a defined severity.
Post-incident reports set out the sequence of events, the root cause and, where known, the vulnerabilities and actors involved.
Responders record the actions they take during an investigation.
The organization protects the integrity and provenance of investigation records.
The organization defines evidence collection and chain-of-custody procedures.
The organization collects incident evidence with metadata and an integrity check, and restricts access to it.
The organization estimates the magnitude of each incident and validates the estimate, for example by sweeping other systems.
The incident response plan lists the internal and external parties to notify and when.
The organization builds contractual and regulatory notification obligations into the plan.
The organization notifies those parties when notification criteria are met and records who and when.
The communications plan states who receives incident information and what may be shared with each.
Leadership receives status updates on major incidents.
Information shared externally follows the agreed sharing rules.
The organization defines containment actions in playbooks for common incident types.
The organization configures automated containment or authorizes a third party in writing to contain on its behalf.
The organization carries out containment and records when it happened.
The organization defines eradication steps in its playbooks.
The organization completes and verifies eradication before closing an incident.
The incident response plan includes a recovery section or links to recovery and continuity plans, triggered from incident response.
The organization documents recovery roles and the authorizations each recovery step needs.
The organization starts recovery from the incident response process and records the hand-off.
Recovery plans set criteria for selecting and prioritizing recovery actions.
The organization performs recovery actions and records their scope, priority and completion.
The organization tests recovery actions on a regular basis.
The recovery procedure requires checking backups and other restoration assets for integrity and compromise before use.
The organization performs and records those integrity checks before restoring.
The organization uses a business impact analysis to set the restoration order of critical functions.
The organization defines how operations run right after an incident, with cybersecurity risk taken into account.
System owners confirm the return to operations after restoration in priority order.
The recovery procedure requires checking restored assets for integrity and confirming normal status before return to production.
The organization performs those checks and the asset owner signs off on restored systems.
The organization documents criteria for declaring the end of incident recovery.
An approver declares the end of recovery and records the date.
The organization completes an after-action report for each incident that reached recovery.
The recovery communication plan names the stakeholders to update and the channel for each.
The organization gives recovery progress updates to leadership and designated stakeholders.
The organization defines an approved procedure for public statements about incident recovery.
Each public recovery statement is issued under that procedure, with approval.
The public-update procedure is linked to the breach notification procedure.
